connect.title: Bridge address
connect.description: Address of the bridge wired to the EasyTouch.

listen.title: Let the bridge connect
listen.description: Point the bridge's TCP client (for example the EW11's Socket A or B) at this Home Assistant's IP address and the port below. Only connections from the bridge address you enter are accepted. The bridge doesn't need to be connected yet: the entities stay unavailable until it dials in.

error.port_in_use: Something on this Home Assistant is already using that port.
error.bad_bridge_host: Enter the bridge's IP address, for example 192.168.1.50.

init.title: Pool controller options

data.power_threshold: Running if power is at least (W)
data.pump_circuits: Pump circuits (what the Pool pump switch turns on)
data.manage_schedules: Manage pump schedules on the controller

data_description.schedule_mode: Only matters with schedule management on. Home Assistant: HA switches the pump and the controller keeps no pump schedules. Controller: HA writes the pump schedules into the controller from the time helpers below and verifies them, and the controller runs the pump on its own.
data_description.power_entity: Optional. When it's reporting, a high-speed relay that's on with no motor draw shows the pool pump as off.
data_description.summer_months: Months that use the summer weekday/weekend times, e.g. 4-10
data_description.source_addr: Leave at 33 unless another remote uses it.
data_description.pump_circuits: The Pool pump switch is made by this integration and switches these circuits as one: on in this order, off in reverse. Usually just 6 (Pool). A two-speed pump wired to the high-speed relay needs Pool and High Speed (6, 2), or the panel drops it after its 5-minute start timer.
data_description.circuit_names: Optional number:name pairs to override the panel's names, e.g. 2:Pump High Speed, 3:Lights
data_description.super_chlor_hours: How long the Super chlorinate switch runs the IntelliChlor at 100%. The controller keeps the pump on for that time.
data_description.manage_schedules: Off (default): nothing is ever written to or cleared from the controller's schedules. On: the integration manages schedules for the pump circuits only. Schedules for any other circuit (lights, heater, AUX) and egg timers are never touched.
data_description.summer_weekday_start: The six time helpers are needed for Controller mode.

init.description:
The Pool pump switch currently turns on: {pump}.

Circuits found on the controller: {circuits}

error.bad_circuits: Enter one or more circuit numbers, e.g. 6 or 6, 2
error.controller_needs_manage: Controller mode writes pump schedules to the controller, so turn on schedule management too.
error.missing_time_helpers: Controller mode needs all six time helpers (summer weekday, summer weekend and winter start/stop). Pick an input_datetime or time entity for each, or choose Home Assistant mode.

schedule_sync_failed.title: Pool controller schedules aren't in sync
schedule_sync_failed.description:
Writing the pump schedule to the EasyTouch didn't work: {error}

It retries every 5 minutes. Check the controller link, the panel and the integration's options.

bridge_address_missing.title: Pool controller: set the bridge address
bridge_address_missing.description: EasyTouch Local is listening on port {port} and accepts a connection from any host, because this entry was set up before the bridge address was asked for. Open Settings → Devices & services → EasyTouch Local → ⋮ → Reconfigure and enter the bridge's IP address; after that only the bridge can connect.
